newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher but gains pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher but gains pared.

text.p: COMEX copper notched up further stock-drop derived gains on Tuesday but the advance was pared by close of trade against a background of slowing U.S. home building.

"We are reminded that copper is ultimately a commodity and moves quickly and dangerously," said Richard Hirsch of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Copper is shaking off the bear spin of the summer and returning to its value."
Copper prices have risen over 15 cents per lb in the past week. The market was supported Tuesday by a 5,050-tonne drop in LME stocks to 96,125 tonnes, their lowest since 1990.
Traders expected stocks to fall 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes, but were surprised when stocks in Singapore fell a nominal 25 tonnes when a hike had been anticipated.
December COMEX settled 0.60 cent up at 106.25 cents per pound, traded 107.60 to 105.10 cents. Volume was heavy at an estimated 24,000 lots, up from Monday's official 14,062 lots.

Although physical traders said U.S. demand was still healthy with even signs of tightness in Europe, U.S. Commerce Dept reported that construction starts of new homes and apartments, a key copper consuming sector, slowed sharply in October to their lowest in a year.
Total starts dropped 5.1 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.366 million.
The starts in September fell by a downwardly revised 6.1 percent, Commerce also reported.
New applications for building permits also declined in October for the third month in a row, hinting at further slowdowns in future starts.
Meanwhile Sumitomo said Tuesday it still retained some copper positions relating to the massive trading losses announced earlier this year.
However, the company added that it did not expect to revise upwards again its estimated loss of $2.6 billion.
